Sponsor: Vice chancellor for research, Kashan University of Medical Sciences

Title: The effects of Multi Minerals (Zn, Mg and Ca) and Vitamins (C and E) Supplementation in the Prevention of Preeclampsia
Collaborator: Student Research Committee, Ilam University of Medical Sciences, Ilam, Iran

Title: Calcium supplementation during pregnancy in low-intake populations
Description:
The purpose of this trial was to determine whether calcium supplementation of pregnant women with low calcium intake reduces pre-eclampsia and preterm delivery. A Multicentre double blind randomised controlled trial. 
Women were assigned randomly to receive:
1. Calcium-containing tablets (1.5 g/d), one tablet three times daily (at meal time, greater than 3 hours after any iron supplements)
2. Indentical placebo

Treatment continued from enrolment to delivery. Treatment was discontinued when magnesium sulphate therapy was initiated to treat pre-eclampsia or when nephrolithiasis was diagnosed, but not when pre-eclampsia or hypertension was diagnosed.
Locations: Argentina; Egypt; India; Peru; South Africa; Switzerland; Viet Nam
Sponsor: UNDP/UNFPA/WHO/World Bank - Special Programme of Research, Development and Research Training in Human Reproduction

Title: WHO randomized trial of calcium supplementation before pregnancy to reduce recurrent pre-eclampsia
Description:
This is a randomized placebo-controlled trial aiming to determine the effect of calcium supplementation before and in the first half of pregnancy on incidence of pre-eclampsia, hypertension and other pregnancy outcomes. Hypothesis: calcium supplementation before pregnancy reduces the incidence of recurrent pre-eclampsia more effectively than supplementation starting at 20 weeks' gestation. 
Experimental Group	Calcium Supplementation	500 mg daily from enrollment	before pregnancy until 20 weeks gestation
Control Group	Control	placebo 500 mg daily	enrolment (before pregnancy) until 20 weeks gestation
Collaborator: University of Zimbabwe; WHO, Dept of Reproductive Health and research; Mowbray Maternity Hospital; Chris Hani Baragwanath Hospital, University of the Witwaterstrand;

Title: Administering cryoprecipitate in obstetric bleeding at an earlier time
Efficacy of eicosapentaenoic acid on the prevention of preterm birth in women with cervical shortening
Description: This is an open-labelled, single-arm, non-randomized trial to determine whether eicosapentaenoic acid supplementation reduce the incidence of preterm birth in women with cervical shortening. The study aims to recruit 128 participants with certical shortening (<=25mm if between 24-28 weeks of gestation, or <=30mm if between 29-33 weeks of gestation. Participants will receive eicosapentaenoic acid 1800mg per day from the day of confirming cervical shortening to 35w6d of gestation or the day of delivery when the deliery occurs before 35w6d.

Title: A randomised controlled trial to study the early preterm delivery in pregnant women between supplemented with 200 mg/day and 1000 mg/day of DHA from second trimester
Description: This is an open-labelled, parallel-arm, randomised controlled trial to compare the proportion of early preterm labour between high dose DHA (1000mg/day) and low dose DHA 200mg/day. The study aims to recruit 1,072 South Asian pregnant women aged 18-40 with singleton pregnancy. Participants will be randomised to receive either 1000mg DHA daily (treatment group) or 200mg DHA daily (control group).
Sponsor: Cloudnine Hospital; Reckitt Benckiser India Pvt Ltd

Title: Effect of vaginally administered docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) fatty acids on pregnancy outcome
Description: This is a single-centre, double-blinded placebo-controlled randomized trial to assess the efficacy of DHA administered vaginally. A total of 60 pregnant womenbetween 18+0 and 24+0 weeks of gestation were recruited. Participants were randomized to receive either 3 g fish oil (1 g DHA) (treatment group) or an identical placebo (control group) applied vaginally daily for 20 weeks starting until delivery.
Sponsor: Italian Society of Prenatal Diagnosis and Fetal Maternal Medicine (S.I.Di.P.) (Italy)

Title: Omega-3 fats to reduce the incidence of prematurity: the ORIP trial
Description:
Early preterm birth (EPTB) is the major cause of perinatal mortality, serious neonatal morbidity and moderate to severe childhood disability in developed countries. Currently, effective broadly applicable primary prevention strategies to reduce the risk of EPTB in the general population are lacking. 
This is a phase IV, parallel arm, double-blinded multi-centre randomised controlled trial to determine whether n-3 LCPUFA supplementation from mid-pregnancy (before 20 weeks gestation) to 34 weeks gestation reduces the risk of EPTB. A total of 5,544 pregnant women were recruited and randomised into receiving either 3 capsules of fish oil (~800 mg of DHA) orally per day (treatment arm) or an identical placebo (control arm) until 34 weeks gestation or birth (whichever occurs first). Participants received intervention from trial entry (<20 weeks) to 34 weeks gestation or birth, whichever comes first, and were be followed up to discharge after birth. The proportion of capsules returned served as a measure of adherence. DHA concentration at the end of intervention was used as an independent biomarker of adherence. The study was conducted over a 5 year period 2013 to 2017.
Sponsor: South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute

Title: A Prospective, Multicenter, Open-label, Single-arm Study to Assess the Effectiveness and Safety of Isoxsuprine Hydrochloride in Women with Preterm Labor in India
Description:
This is a prospective, multicenter, open-label, single-arm study to assess the effectiveness and safety of isoxsuprine hydrochloride for preterm labour. The study aims to recruit 245 pregnant women aged 18 years and above diagnosed, who were diagnosed with preterm labour and prescribed isoxsuprine hydrochloride (Duvadilan®) by the physician during the routine practice.

Post Marketing Observational Study

Title: Isoxsuprine in prevention of preterm labor
Description: This is a phase III, double-blind, parallel-arm, prospective randomized trial to assess the efficacy of isoxupine for preterm labour. A total of 81 pregnant singleton with intact foetal membrane in women between 26 to 34 weeks of gestation and with labour pain. Pregnant women with premature rupture of membrane, chorioamnionitis, antepartum haemorrhage and systemic diseases were excluded. After stopping the contractions with IV magnesium sulfate participants were randomized to receive either oral Isoxuprine 10mg TDS (treatment arm) or an identical placebo (control arm) until 34 weeks of gestation.
Sponsor: Vice-chancellor for research of Hormozgan University of Medical Sciences

Title: To evaluate efficacy and safety of Isoxsuprine Hydrochloride in females with preterm labor.
Description:
This is a prospective, single center, open-label, non-comparative study designed to evaluate effectiveness and safety of Isoxsuprine hydrochloride as a uterine relaxant in preterm labor. A total of 50 pregnant women aged 18-45 years with preterm labour were recruited, admitted at the study site and are clinically indicated for the treatment with Isoxsuprine hydrochloride, as per the discretion of treating physician.
All study participants were given a loading dose of intravenous infusion of Isoxsuprine hydrochloride four (4) ampoules (40 mg) in 500 ml of 5% dextrose giving a concentration of 0.8 mg/ml. Drop rate will be set at 8 drops/minute (0.04 mg/minute). The drop rate will be increased by 8 drops/minute after every 15-minutes until uterine quiescence is attained, or patient develops adverse effects like maternal tachycardia (heart rate >130/minute) or hypotension (systolic blood pressure <80 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure <40 mmHg), or intolerable nausea and vomiting or foetal tachycardia (foetal heart rate >160 beats/minute). The infusion was discontinued if any adverse effect develops, otherwise, intravenous infusion was continued over next 12 hours after uterine quiescence. After 15 minutes of stoppage of infusion, intramuscular injection of Isoxsuprine hydrochloride 10 mg/ 4 hourly was given up to first 24-hours of hospitalization. Subsequently, Isoxsuprine hydrochloride 40mg sustained release capsule was prescribed twice daily as maintenance therapy for next 24-hours, and the patient was kept on the same dose till the time of the delivery.
Treatment was considered successful if the uterine quiescence was maintained for at least 48 hours. If the sign of preterm labor recurs, parenteral therapy as described above would be started. Adverse effects reported or observed were recorded. Treatment was discontinued if the patient experienced intolerable side effects requiring discontinuation of the therapy. Otherwise, the patient was be prescribed Isoxsuprine hydrochloride 40mg sustained release capsule, twice daily as maintenance therapy till the time of delivery.

Title: Effect of Celebrex in prevention of preterm labor
Description: This is a single-blinded, parallel-arm randomized study to evaluate Celebrex’s efficacy in preventing the inflammatory process leading to preterm delivery. A total of 200 pregnant women with preterm labor aged 16-44 years were recruited. Participant were randomized to two groups. The treatment group received Celebrex 100 mg orally initially, following the repeated same dose every 12 hours with the cumulative dose of 400 mg if the contractions continue (treatment arm). The control group received Magnesium sulfate with the initial dose of 4 grams and then 2 grams per hour, increased to 3 grams per hour if the contractions continue. Either uterine contractions persist maximally 48 hours after the beginning of the treatment or the drug side effects make the patient to ask for the treatment termination, it will be considered as nonresponsive and the medications will be discontinued.
Sponsor: Vice Chancellor for research, Kashan University of Medical Sciences

Title: the efficace of magnesium sulfate in preterm labor pain managment
Description: This is a single-blinded, parallel-arm randomized trial to compare efficacy of maintenance therapy and continuous intravenous therapy with magnesium sulfate in preterm labor pain management. A total of 70 pregnant women with gestational age of 26 to 34 weeks and with threanted preterm labour were recruited. articipants were randomized to receive 4gr magnesium sulfate in 200cc D/W 5% during 15 to 20 minutes, either as a continuous infusion therapy with 20 gr MS in 10 hours (infusion group) or maintenance therapy with 2gr/hr MS for 12 hours (maintenance group).Patients who did response to magnesium sulfate within 2 h were excluded. The success rate in both groups for stopping labor pain, NICU admission, pregnancy duration and APGAR score at 5 min were assessed.

Title: Comparing the effectiveness of Nifedipine and magnesium sulfate in treating preterm labor.
Description: This is an open-labelled, parallel-arm clinical study to compare the effectiveness of nifedipine and magnesium sulfate in treating preterm labor. A total of 110 pregnant women with preterm labor at their 27th-36th week of gestation were recruited and assigned to two groups. The Nifedipine group received 10 mg of nifedipine orally repeated up to 4 doses per 20/min which was continued by 20mg/4-8hr and then every 12 hours till 48hr or 12hr after clinical responses. The Magnesium sulfate group received 4gr/20min of magnesium sulfate intravenously which continued by 1g/hr up to 24hr, in case of no contraindications treatment continued till 24hr or for 24hr after clinical responses. If no contractions were observed it was considered as clinical response. Headache, hypotension, dyspnea and tachycardia considered as maternal complications and neonatal outcome was described by 1st min Apgar score.
Sponsor: urmia university of medical sciences, deputy of research and technology.

Title: Magnesium sulfate and nifedipine on treatment of preterm labor
Description: This is an open-labelled randomized trial to compare the effect of nifedipine and magnesium sulfate for treatment of preterm labor. A total of 100 singleton pregnant women between 24 to 37 weeks of gestation with signs of preterm labor referred to Alzahra hospital in 2003 were recruited. Women were randomized in two groups. In the nifedipine group, participants were given nifedipine (10 mg) sublingual plus another capsule every 15 minutes if uterine contractions persisted, until a maximum dose of 40mg for one hour. Depending on tocolytic effects of nifedipine that was used during one hour, a minimal dose of 60 mg every day was used. After 3 days, the dose would be decreased gradually and patient would receive 20 mg/day nifedipine up to 36 weeks of gestation. In the Magnesium sulfate group, participants were given intravenous magneisum sulfate heptahydrate 20% with a loading dose of 4 gram during 30 minutes, followed by a maintenance dose of 2 gr/hr until stopping or reducing uterine contractions. Vital signs, vaginal bleeding, rupture of membranes, fetal heart rate, and uterine contractions were monitored.
Sponsor: Vice Chancellor for Research, Guilan University of Medical Sciences

Title: Is intramuscular progesterone as effective as oral nifedipine for treating threatened preterm labor?
Description: This is a double-blinded, parallel-arm randomized trial to compare the tocolytic effect of 300 milligram intramuscular progesterone with oral nifedipine on threatened preterm labor A total of 497 pregnant women aged 18-45, with threatened preterm labour were recruited Participants were randomized to receive 200 mg intramuscular progestrone (100 mg in each gluteus maximus) or oral nifedipine (loading dose of 30 mg and continued with 10-20 mg every 4-6 hours until pain relief) as tocolytic agents.

Title: Treating Preterm Labor by Nifedipine or Magnesium sulfate
Description: This is an open-labelled, parallel-arm, randomized study to compare nifedipin and magnesium sulfate in the management of preterm labor. A total of 100 pregnant women between 24-37 week gestations with preterm labour were recruited and randomized into two groups. The Nifedipine group received 30 mg nifedipine for the first dose and then 10 mg/6 hours. The Magnesum sulfate group received 10 g magnesium sulfate for the first dose and 5 g/4 hours. After 7 days, two groups were compared for duration of gestation and side effects of treatment.

Title: Effect of Nifedipin and magnesium sulfate on preterm labor
Description: This is a randomized single-blind and two centers clinical trial to compare the effect of nifedipine and magnesium sulfate on labor pain. A total of 200 pegnant women with singleton pregnancy and diagnosed with preterm labour were recruited and randomized into two groups. Before treatment, both groups were hydrated with 1 liter Ringer serum. In the Magnesium sulfate group, 4 grams magnesium sulfate in 200 cc Ringer serum was infused for 20 minutes and then 2 grams per hour for up to 24 hours or 2 hours after contraction. In the Nifedipine group, 10 mg oral nifedipine was administered and if contractions continue for 15 minutes, the second dose was administered and continued every quarter of an hour for 1 hour. After that, one 10 mg Nifedipin capsule per 6 hours was administered for up to 24 hours. The amount of uterine contractions was compared in both groups.
Sponsor: Vice chancellor for research, Zahedan University of Medical Science

Title: Magnesium Sulfate In Adverse With Nifedipine In suppression preterm labor In Pregnant With Preterm Labor
Description: This is a double-blinded, parallel-arm, placebo-controlled randomized trial to assess the efficacy of magnesium sulfate in suppressing preterm labor and prevent mortality and morbidity of fetus and neonate. A total of 80 pregnant women aged 14-45 years with preterm labour were recruited and randomized into two treatment groups. The Magnesium sulfate group will be given 4 gram Magnesium Sulfate as a loading dose then continuing with 2 gram every hour until 48 hours. The Nifedipine group will be given Nifedipine tablet (20mg), followed by another 20 mg Nifedipine tablet after half an hour if contractions persist, and then continuing with 20mg Nifedipin every 3-8 hours until contractions subside.

Title: comparison of efficacy of indomethacin and magnesium sulphate in prevention of preterm labour
Description: This is an open-labelled, parallel-arm randomized trial to compare the effects of indomethacin and magnesium sulfate in delaying delivery and compare maternal and neonatal outcome associated with the effects of the two drugs. A total of 150 pregnant women with a gestational age of 32-28 with a diagnosis of preterm labor admitted to Tabriz Alzahra hospitl were recruited and randomized to two groups. The Magnesium sulfate group received magnesium sulfate 4 g intravenously within 20 minutes, continued with 2 gr IV infusion until the reduction or cessation of contractions. The Indomethacin group received indomethacin suppository, initially 50 mg and then 50 mg every 6 hours until 24 hours. Time delay in delivery and maternal morbidity and neonatal complications in two groups were monitored.
Sponsor: Vice chancellor for research,Tabriz University of Medical Sciences

Title: Comprasion of nifedipin versus magnesium salfate in Treatment of preterm labor
Description: This is an open-labelled, parallel-arm, randomized trial is compare Nifedipin versus Magnesium Sulfate in treatment of preterm labor. A total of 120 pregnant women admitted in Rohani Hospital of Babol with preterm labor were recruited and randomly assigned to two groups. The magnesium sulfate group received  4gr bolus and follow by 2gr/h infusion, continued until 12 hours after stopping of contraction. Nifedipine group received 10mg orally every 20 minutes for total 5 doses and assess for blood pressure, followed by 20 mg orally every 6 hours until 24 hours and every 8 hours until next 24 hours. The first step of management is bed rest and hydration by 500cc infusion of ringer solution and 50 mg Pethedine IM for two groups. If contractions are continued, all patients would receive Betamethasone 12mg IM twice, 24 hours apart and then nifedipine or magnesium sulfate.
Sponsor: Vice Chancellor for Research and Technology, Babol University of Medical Sciences

Title: A randomised clinical trial of different infusion rates of magnesium sulphate given prenatally to women.
Description: This is a single-blinded, randomized controllied trial. A total of 51 female participants from South Australia were recruited and received a magnesium sulphate intravenous infusion for 24 hours or until they give birth (whichever is the shorter). The participants were randomised to different rates of administration of the intravenous loading infusion. 4 g magnesium sulphate over 60 minutes followed by 1 g per hour versus 4 g magnesium sulphate over 20 minutes followed by 1 g per hour.
Sponsor: ARCH: Australian Research Centre for Health of Women and Babies, The Robinson Institute, The University of Adelaide

Title: Effect of magnesium sulfate and nifedipine in preterm labor
Description: This is a phase II, double-blinded, parallel-arm randomized trial to compare the effect of nifedipine and magnesium sulfate in the treatment of preterm labor. A total of 100 pregnant women with a gestational age of 28-34 weeks and with preterm labor pain were recruited and randomized into two groups. The Nifedipine group received nifedipine with an initial dose of 20 mg orally and then every 6 hours for 24 hours. The Magnesium sulfate group received 20% magnesium sulfate with an initial dose of 4 gram intravenously and then 2 gram per hour for 24 hours.

Title: A Comparison of nitroglycerine skin patch and sublingual tablets of isosorbide di-nitrate for prevention of preterm labor
Description: The is a single-blinded randomized clinical trial to compare the efficacy of TNG skin patch and isosorbide dinitrate for prevention of preterm labour. A total of 110 pregnant women admitted to Asali hospital were recruited and first given maintenance treatment upon contract. If uterine contractions continue, the participants would be randomized to two groups. In the TNG group, participants received a 10-mg TNG skin patch to the lateral arm. If the contractions continue after 1 hour, another skin patch would be used one hour later on the same location. In the Isosorbide dinitrate group, participants were given isosorbide dinitrate 5 mg sublingual tablets every half an hour (up to 8 doses). If the contractions are cut off, Isosorbide dinitrate 10 mg tablets would be given to the patients one hour later, continued every 6 hours up to 48 hours. Response to the treatment was defined as cessation of contractions and lack of labour progress.
Sponsor: Lorestsn University Of Medical Sciences. Lorestan, Iran

Title: The effect of isosorbide dinitrate in preventing of severe pre-eclampsia
Description: This study aim was to evaluate the effect of isosorbide dinitrate in the prevention of severe preeclampsia in patients with mild preeclampsia. Twenty seven women with single tone pregnancy with gestational age of 36-26 weeks and the diagnosis of mild preeclampsia were enrolled in the study and were assigned into intervention or control groups. Intervention group received 10 mg of isosorbide dinitrate oral tablet three times a day and the control group received no treatment. Delay in symptoms of severe preeclampsia and gestation duration in both groups were measured and compared between groups.

Title: Comparison examination of microbiota in mouth, intestine and vagina before and after medication of a raw bacillus agent (an active bacterial probiotics, Bio-Three) to the threatened premature delivery patient who requires in-hospital treatment, and examination about validity of preterm delivery medical treatment
Description: This is an open-blinded, single-arm, non-randomized trial to perform a raw bacillus agent (Bio-Three®, 6 tablets per day) medication to patients of threatened preterm delivery who need in-hospital treatment and to evaluate a change of microbiota in mouth, intestine and vagina before and after medication by the T-RFLP (Terminal restriction fragment length polymorphism) method and meta-genomics analysis using a next-generation sequencer. The study aimed to recruit 60  pregnant women with threatened preterm delivery (tocolysis index, 2 to 6). Participanst received Bio-Three 6 tablets per day for 14 days.

Title: Comparison of probiotics in the prevention of preterm labor
Description: This is a phase III, single-blinded, parallel-arm, randomized trial to compare the effects of vaginal and oral probiotics in the prevention of preterm labor. The study aims to recruit 185 pregnant women with gestation age >=25 weeks admitted to Kamali Hospital. Participants will be randomized into three groups. The first group will receive probiotic tablets, daily from 25 weeks of pregnancy until 37 weeks of gestation. The second group will receive a probiotic vaginal capsule, daily from 25 weeks of pregnancy until 37 weeks of gestation, and the third group will not receive any intervention. The final outcome of the study will be assessed by a third party who is unaware of the study process. Also, the statistician will be unaware of the study process

Title: Investigation of the effects of vaginal probiotic capsules on prolonging the time of membrane rupture up to delivery and on maternal and fetal complications.
Description: This is an open-labelled, parallel-arm, randomized study to investigate the effects of vaginal probiotic capsules on prolonging the time of membrane rupture up to delivery and on maternal and fetal complications. A total of 64 pregnant women with sington pregnancy admitted to Ghaem, Emam Reza and Ommolbanin hospitals were recruited and randomized to receive either one vaginal probiotic capsule daily for 10 days (treatment group) or no probiotics (control group). Mother's vital signs and fetus health were precisely controlled through daily NST, sonography twice a week and CBC every other day. 2 weeks after delivery, infants and mothers in both groups were assessed for outcomes.

Title: A feasibility study investigating pravastatin for the prevention of preterm birth in women
Description: This is a Phase II, double-blinded, placebo-controlled randomized controlled trial assess efficacy of pravastatin when compared to placebo in prolonging time to delivery, reducing contractions and inflammation in both the mother and fetus in women with preterm labour. A total of 40 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies and with gestational age between 24+0 and 35+6 weeks were recruited. Participants were randomized to receive either Pravastatin 40mg (treatment arm) or an identical placebo (control arm) once daily for 7 days.

Title: A comparative study on the efficacy of nifedipine/Indomethacin combination and nifedipine monotherapy for prevention of preterm birth in Sudanese pregnant women
Description: This is an open-labelled, parallel-arm, single-centered randomized trial to compare the efficacy and safety profile of nifedipine/Indomethacin combination versus nifedipine monotherapy for prevention of preterm birth in Sudanese pregnant women. The study aims to recruit 346 pregnant women diagnosed as threatened preterm labour patient and with gestational age between 25 and 34 weeks. Participants will be randomized into two groups. The monotherapy group will receive 20 mg oral nifedipine combined with a rectal placebo. If contractions inhibition occurs for two hours, the patient will continue receiving 20 mg of oral nifedipine four hours for 48 h, the maximum dose should not exceed 180 mg per day. Rectal placebo will be repeated after 90 min of the first dosage and then it will be prescribed every 4 h. The combination group will receive 20 mg oral nifedipine and 100 mg rectal indomethacin. In the case of inhibiting contractions after two hours, the patient will receive 25 mg of oral indomethacin and 20 mg of oral nifedipine every four hours for 24 hours. The maximum daily dosage will not exceed 200 mg/day for indomethacin and 180 mg per day for nifedipine with a maximum duration of 48 hours. Antenatal corticosteroids will be provided according to the guidelines

Title: preterm labor inhibition
Description: This is a phase IIl, parallel-arm, double-blinded, placebo-controlled randomized trial to compare the effect of co-administration of magnesium sulfate-indomethacin with magnesium sulfate alone in labor inhibition Early in Kosar Hospital. The study aims to recruit 200 pregnant women with singleton pregnancy with gestation age of 24-32 weeks referring to Kosar Hospital for preterm labour. Participants will be randomized into two groups. The treatment group received intravenous magnesium sulfate at a loading dose of 4-6 gr and then 2gr per hour until maximum 48 hours or till 12 hours after the end of contractions and indomethacin 100mgr suppository applied twice daily for two days. The control group will receive the same dose of magnesium sulfate plus an identical placebo suppository applied twice daily for two days.

Title: A comparison of the 2 methods for the treatment of preterm labor
Description: This was a open-labelled, parallel-group, randomized trial to compare the effect of Indometacine and Nifedipine for the treatment of patients who would be admitted in the labor ward because of preterm labor. A total of 50 pregnant women diagnosed with preterm labour were recruited and randomized assigned into two groups. The nifedipine group received an initial dose of 10mg (one capsule) sublingually every 20 minutes for four doses. If the contractions are inhibited, Nifedipin would becontinued orally (20 mg) every 6 hours for the first 24 hours, and then every 8 hours for the following 24 hours, and finally 10mg every 8 hours for the last 24 hours. If the contractions continue and the dilatation of the cervix was progressing, or the blood pressure decreases below 90/50 mmHg, the use of Nifedipin would be discontinued. During this period, patients would be monitored for uterine contractions and also for any possible side effects. For the indomethacin group, participans were given 100 mg (one suppository) rectally and if the contractions continue, the same dose would be repeated 1 hour later. The maximum daily dose of Indometacine was 200 mg/day and the maximum duration of its use was 48 hours. Corticosteroids in the form of Bethametasone would be administered intramuscularly; 12mg every 24 hours for 48 hours in both groups, and then all patients would be monitored for the evaluation of the tocolytic’s effects. The uterine contractions would be checked every 15 minutes during the first 24 hours and then every 4-6 hours. Response to treatment would be defined as inhibiting of uterine contractions during the first 2 hours and then for 48 hours and for 7 days.
Sponsor: Iran University of Medical Sciences, Deputy of Research and Technology

Title: comparison of efficacy of indomethacin and magnesium sulphate in prevention of preterm labour
Description: This is an open-labelled, parallel-arm randomized trial to compare the effects of indomethacin and magnesium sulfate in delaying delivery and compare maternal and neonatal outcome associated with the effects of the two drugs. A total of 150 pregnant women with a gestational age of 32-28 with a diagnosis of preterm labor admitted to Tabriz Alzahra hospitl were recruited and randomized to two groups. The Magnesium sulfate group received magnesium sulfate 4 g intravenously within 20 minutes, continued with 2 gr IV infusion until the reduction or cessation of contractions. The Indomethacin group received indomethacin suppository, initially 50 mg and then 50 mg every 6 hours until 24 hours. Time delay in delivery and maternal morbidity and neonatal complications in two groups were monitored.
Sponsor: Vice chancellor for research,Tabriz University of Medical Sciences

Title: Treatment of preterm labor
Description: This is a triple-blinded, parallel-arm, placebo-controlled randomized trial to compare the efficacy of two tocolytic agents; nifedipine and indomethacin; for inhibiting preterm uterine contractions as monotherapy and combination therapy. A total of 150 pregnant women aged 18-40 years with spontaneous preterm labour were recruited and randomly assigned to 3 groups.  Group A; 100 mg rectal indomethacin was administered along with an oral placebo. Group B; 20 mg oral nifedipine was administered along with a rectal placebo. Group C; a combination of rectal indomethacin and oral nifedipine was administered. The primary outcome was delivery after 48 hours and deliveries before 34 weeks of gestation.

Title: Long-term follow-up of children exposed in utero to low-dose aspirin for prevention of preterm birth, a follow-up of the APRIL trial
Description: This is a long-term prospective cohort study of 4-year old children born to mothers from the APRIL trial to assess the long-term effect of in-utero exposure to low-dose aspirin compared to placebo on child (neuro)development, behavior and health. The original trial was a double-blinded, parallel-arm, placebo-controlled randomized trial in which participants  were randomized between low-dose aspirin (80 mg) and placebo. .Study medication started between 8- and 16-weeks gestation and continued up to 36 weeks gestation or delivery, whichever came first. The study aims to recruit 200 children at four years' corrected age who were born to mothers from the APRIL trial (n=406).

Title: Effect of Aspirin in prevention of preterm labor
Description: This is a double-blinded, parallel-arm, randomized trial to compare the effectiveness of 80 and 150 mg aspirin on prevention preterm labor in high risk pregnant women in first trimester of pregnancy. A total of  100 high risk pregnant women aged 18-40 years with preterm labor based on first trimester doppler sonography were recruited and randomized to receive either 80mg aspirin (low-dose) or 100mg (high-dose) from 11-13 week of pregnancy until 34 week or delivery time.

Title: Aspirin Effect in the Prevention of Preterm Labor in Patient with Previous Spontaneous Preterm Birth
Description: This is a phase III, open-labelled, parallel-arm randomized trial to assess the efficacy of aspirin in the prevention of preterm labor in patient with previous spontaneous preterm birth. A total of 380 pregnant women with singleton pregnancy with gestation age of 8-16 weeks and history of spontaneous preterm birth referred to Mahdieh and Shohada hospitals were recruited. Paticipants were randomized to receive eiehter 80mg daily aspirin (treatment group) or no aspirin (control group). Routine prenatal visits will be made for both groups. Information about pregnancy and childbirth care, including gestational age at delivery, baby weight and Apgar, will be recorded. The data will be collected using a data log checklist.
Sponsor: Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences

Title: Effect of administration low dose aspirin on pregnancy outcome
Description: This is a single-blinded, parallel-arm, randomized trial to evaluate the effect of low ‎dose aspirin (80 milligram) administration on pregnancy outcome in those complicated with unexplained increased Alpha-‎fetoprotein. A total of 200 pregnant women with singleton pregnancy and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) value ≥ 2.50 MoM were recruited. Participants were randomized to receive either low dose Aspirin (80 mg) administrated from study time until 34 weeks of pregnancy (treatment group) or no treatment (control group). The outcome of pregnancy on preterm birth, fetal death, preeclampsia, fetal growth restriction (IUGR) and neonatal admission were assessed.

Title: Aspirin for the prevention of preterm delivery in patients with prophylactic cervical cerclage
Description: This is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of aspirin for the prevention of preterm delivery in patients with prophylactic cervical cerclage, assess the efficacy of maternal-infant safety and efficacy cost ratio, and provide a reliable scientific basis for the efficacy of aspirin in the prevention and treatment of pregnancy. The study aims to recruit 200 pregnant women aged 18-40 years who are diagnosed with cervical insufficiency. The participants will be randomized to receive either aspirin 75mg per day (treatment arm) or an identical placebo (control arm).
Sponsor: Women's Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine

Title: Aspirin for the prevention of preterm delivery in patients with prophylactic cervical cerclage
Description: This is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of aspirin in the treatment of pregnancy complicated with adenomyosis to reduce the incidence of premature delivery, to provide a new therapeutic target for the prevention and treatment of premature delivery and adverse pregnancy outcomes, and to fill in the blank of effective prevention of premature delivery in pregnancy with adenomyosis at home and abroad. The study aims to recruit 450 pregnant women with singleton pregnancy who are diagnosed with adenomyosis. The participants will be randomized to receive either aspirin (treatment arm) or an identical placebo (control arm).
Sponsor: Women's Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine

Title: The effect of Low-dose aspirin on cervical length as an indicator of preterm delivery in nulliparous pregnant women that has been referred to gynecology clinic in Semnan
Description: This is a double-blinded, paralle-arm, placebo-controlled, single-centered randomized trial to assess the effect of low-dose aspirin on cervical length as an indicator of preterm delivery in nulliparous pregnant women. A total of 60 nulliparous pregnant women aged 18-40 years were recruited and randomized to receive either 80mg aspirin daily (treatment group) or an identical placebo (control group), in combination with folic acid and iron tablets from the second trimester up to 32 weeks of pregnancy. The cervical length and also blood hemoglobin were measured once a time at 13 weeks and once again at 30 weeks of pregnancy.
Sponsor: Vice Chancellor for Research and Technology, Semnan University of Medical Sciences

Title: Low dose aspirin in the Prevention of Recurrent Spontaneous Preterm Labour
Description: This is a phase IV, double-blinded, placebo-controlled, multi-centre randomized controlled trial to assess the effectiveness of low dose aspirin compared with placebo in the prevention of recurrent spontaneous preterm birth. A total of 406 pregnant women aged >=18 years with history of spontaneous preterm birth were recruited. Participants were randomized to receive either Aspirin 80mg per day (treatment arm) or an identical placebo (control arm).

Title: Effect of lactoferrin for vaginitis and cervicitis in obstetrics

Title: Low Dose Aspirin for Preventing Intrauterine Growth Restriction and Preeclampsia in Sickle Cell Pregnancy (PIPSICKLE)
Description: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a haemoglobinopathy fraught with complications as a result of vaso-occlusion, thrombosis and chronic anaemia. Pregnancy in sickle cell disease aggravates already existing pathophysiological mechanisms in affected women. It worsens anaemia and the resultant chronic hypoxia, increases the risk of infections, worsens vasoconstriction and alters procoagulation mechanisms. As a result, sickle cell pregnancies are often complicated by preeclampsia, stillbirths, preterm deliveries, intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), and an increase in their usual crises and chest infections. Women with sickle cell disease therefore have a high incidence of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. In the general population, low dose aspirin is known to decrease the risk of cardiovascular events and to prevent platelet clumping thus enhancing free flow of erythrocytes. In a previous study we found a reversal in prostacyclin-thromboxane ratio in pregnant SCD women, a situation that is also found in non-sickle pregnancies with preeclampsia and unexplained IUGR (1). Low dose aspirin (LDA) has been found to reduce the incidence of pre-eclampsia and IUGR in high-risk women due to its reduction of vasoconstrictor thromboxane whilst sparing prostacyclin, in effect correcting the ratio (2). It has been found to be safe and is used extensively in pregnancy (2) but has not been tested specifically in sickle cell pregnancy. We hypothesize that LDA would reduce the incidence of IUGR and preeclampsia in pregnant SCD women. Objectives are: 1. To determine effect of LDA use during pregnancy in HbSS and HbSC women on risk of IUGR, perinatal death or miscarriage 2. To determine effect of LDA use during pregnancy in HbSS and HbSC women on risk of maternal complications including preeclampsia, preterm delivery, number of vaso-occlusive crises, etc 3. To build capacity in conducting RCTs

Description:

The biologic effect of low-dose aspirin on platelet function in this population with respect to variables that may affect bioavailability (maternal body mass index, gestational age, compliance) will also be measured..

Title: The carboprost or oxytocin postpartum haemorrhage effectiveness study
Description:

Title: The EPPI Trial – Enoxaparin for the Prevention of Preeclampsia and Intrauterine growth restriction – a pilot randomised open-label trial.
Description: Preeclampsia and fetal intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) are common complications during pregnancy that can cause long lasting health effects for mother and baby in later life. It is believed both conditions are caused by abnormal development of the placenta (whenua/after-birth) and can often recur in future pregnancies. There are several therapies that have been studied to prevent these diseases but, until now, none have been proven to be very effective. Heparin is a drug that prevents blood clots and is believed to help the placenta to develop well. Some studies have suggested that heparin may reduce the risk of preeclampsia and IUGR but this has not been properly assessed in a randomised trial. Our study will invite women who have had a previous pregnancy severely affected by these conditions. Half of the women will be given the heparin injection each day as well as current standard of care (aspirin for all women and calcium for women with previous preeclampsia) and the other half will receive the current standard of care. All women will be monitored very closely. At the end of the study we will be able to assess if the heparin injections reduce the risk of preeclampsia and IUGR.

Title: The administration of fibrinogen concentrate (a component of blood involved in clotting process) to be given to those women who, after delivery of babies, develop severe bleeding to establish if this drug will prevent further blood loss or reduce the volu
Description:
Severe bleeding after delivery is a worldwide cause of mothers dying during childbirth. We can identify some of those woman at risk but in most cases there is no indication that a woman may bleed. We suspect in those cases the severe bleeding that develop is due to a low level of a clotting factor called Fibrinogen in their blood. Studies have demonstrated that there is a link between low level of fibrinogen (that helps blood clot) and those woman that have severe bleeding after delivery. We hope that to correct the level of fibrinogen will prevent severe bleeding.

Intervention Arm: Fibrinogen; fibrinogen concentrate 4g given intra-venously upfront in women after delivery with a post partum blood loss of more than 1000mls and with signs of ongoing bleeding.
Control Arm: Placebo; Saline intravenously in women after delivery with a post partum blood loss of more than 1000mls and with signs of ongoing bleeding.

The study is estimated to enrol 245 participants and will take place in New Zealand.

Title: Fibrinogen concentrate to treat bleeding at the time of childbirth
Description:
This study aims to establish whether giving fibrinogen (one of the body's blood clotting factors and it plays an important role is forming a strong clot) to women who are bleeding during childbirth and who have a low fibrinogen, reduces blood loss and reduces the amount of blood transfusion that women require.

Control Arm: Placebo; Placebo will be 50 mL of normal saline for each 1 gm of fibrinogen.
Intervention Arm: Fibrinogen; 1 gm fibrinogen concentrate as a lyophilised powder in a blinded bottle and 50ml sterile water for injection in a diluent bottle. 
The dose of fibrinogen/placebo will be rounded to use complete vials and the maximum dose of fibrinogen or placebo will not exceed 8 gm.

The study will recruit 663 participants and will be undertaken at multiple centres in the United Kingdom.

Intervention Arm 2: Ergometrine; parturient received intravenously injected ergometrine 0.2 mg immediately after birth of anterior shoulder.

The study will enrol 80 participants, and will take place in Thailand.
Sponsor: Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Faculty of Medicine Ramathibodi Hospital.

Title: Carbetocin for preventing excessive bleeding after birth.
Description:
The World Health Organization is coordinating the implementation of “A Phase III, Randomized, Double-blind, Active controlled, Multinational, Multicentric, Non-inferiority trial using Carbetocin room temperature stable (RTS) and Oxytocin for the Prevention of Postpartum Hemorrhage during the Third Stage of Labour in Women Delivering Vaginally”. The primary endpoint for assessing the non-inferiority of Carbetocin RTS in the WHO multi-centric trial will be the composite outcome of “blood loss of 500 ml or more or the use of additional uterotonics” at one hour and up to two hours for women who continue to bleed after one hour within a non-inferiority margin of 1.16 on the relative risk scale.
Although measured postpartum blood loss has been used as the primary outcome in a number of trials assessing the efficacy of strategies for prevention and treatment of PPH, post-delivery hemoglobin and decline from pre-delivery level have been regarded as more appropriate alternatives because they are theorized to be stronger indicators of risk for shock and death than postpartum blood loss. However, there are no studies assessing the effect of Carbetocin RTS for prevention of postpartum hemorrhage in vaginal deliveries with post-delivery hemoglobin as the primary outcome. World Health Organization encourages site PIs to conduct additional sub-studies including dissertations/theses within the framework of the main trial as part of their efforts at research capacity building. Hence, the proposed nested randomized controlled trial will test the efficacy of the two drugs for preventing PPH in vaginal births on change in post-delivery hemoglobin adjusted for pre-delivery hemoglobin. The trial is adequately powered to test this secondary hypothesis on the 1,400 participants (out of the total 30,000 participants to be recruited globally to the WHO multi-centric trial) who will be recruited to the trial at the Belgaum, India site.

Intervention Arm: Carbetocin Room Temperature Stable; 100 μg/mL IM will be administered as a single IM dose of 100 μg (in a 1 mL solution)within one minute of birth of the baby after ascertaining that there is no second fetus.
Comparator Arm: Oxytocin; single IM dose of 10 IU (in a 1 mL solution) within one minute of birth of the baby after ascertaining that there is no second fetus.

The study will enrol 1799 participants, and will take place at hospitals in India.
Locations: Egypt; Nigeria; Kenya; Argentina; Brazil; Thailand; Singapore; Uganda; South Africa; United Kingdom; India

Description:
A phase III, randomized, double-blind, active, controlled, multinational, multicentre, non-inferiority trial using Carbetocin room temperature stable (RTS) for the prevention of postpartum haemorrhage during the third stage of labour in women delivering vaginally.

Experimental Arm: Carbetocin - heat/stable; 100 µg IM after vaginal delivery.
Active Comparator: Oxytocin; 10 UI IM after vaginal delivery.

The study will recruit 30000 participants, and will take place at 23 sites across Argentina, Brazil, Egypt, India, Kenya, Nigeria, Singapore, South Africa, Thailand, Uganda and the United Kingdom.

Title: Carbetocin for preventing excessive bleeding after birth.
Description: This Phase III study is proposed to show the non-inferiority of carbetocin room temperature stable (RTS) 100 µg intramuscular (IM) versus oxytocin 10 IU IM for preventing postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) in women delivering vaginally. The study will take approximately 24 months to complete and will be performed as a multi-national, double-blind, parallel group study, in accordance with the study protocol. Globally, this study is proposed to be conducted in 10 countries including United Kingdom, South Africa, Uganda, Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt, Singapore, Thailand, Argentina, and India.Intervention Arm: RTS Carbetocin; 100 µg solution Route of administration: Intramuscular (IM) InjectionComparator Arm: Oxytocin; 10 IU solution Intramuscular (IM)  We propose to conduct the above referenced study on 7100 subjects at 06 study centers in India, out of an approximately 30,000 planned subjects to be enrolled globally.

Title: Carbetocin versus Oxytocin for the Prevention of Postpartum Hemorrhage in Gestational Diabetic Women Undergoing Cesarean Section
Description:
Postpartum hemorrhage is the most commonly encountered cause of maternal mortality especially in developing countries. It leads to a prolonged hospital stay, additional treatments, and psychological impact on the patients and their families incurring extra-costs. Gestational diabetes is a risk factor for its occurrence. Active management of the third stage (using oxytocin or carbetocin) of labor decreased the incidence of such catastrophe. This study aimed at assessment of the efficacy of carbetocin in reducing the amount of blood loss in gestational diabetic pregnant women delivered by cesarean section.

Experimental Arm: Carbetocin; 100 µg carbetocin diluted in 500 ml of Ringer’s lactate solution injected slowly into the vein over 20 min (Pabal; Ferring, Langley, UK).
Active Comparator: Oxytocin; 5 IU oxytocin (Syntocinon; Alliance, Chippenham, UK) in 500 ml of Ringer’s lactate solution injected slowly into the vein over 20 min.

The study is estimated to recruit 160 participants, and will take place in Egypt.
Sponsor: Faculty of Medicine, Suez Canal University

Title: Assessment of the efficacy of using intraumbilical vein injection of oxytocin after delivery of newborn in reducing postpartum hemorrhage
Description:
The aim of this study is to assess the efficacy of using intraumbilical vein injection of oxytocin in active management of the third stage of labor.

Experimental Arm: 10 IU of oxytocin diluted in 9cc ringer by intraumbilical vein injection and 10cc ringer by peripheral vein injection.
Comparator Arm: 10cc ringer by intraumbilical vein injection and 10 IU of oxytocin diluted in 9cc ringer by peripheral vein injection.
Both groups to recieve 20 units of oxytosin diluted in 1 liter of ringer after delivery.

The study will recruit 200 participants, and take place at a hospital in Iran.

Title: Post partum haemorrhage (PPH) prevention: oxytocin pharmacokinetics and maternal body mass index (BMI).
Description:
Correlative assessment of prophylactic oxytocin pharmacokinetics (PK) to maternal body mass index (BMI) following intravenous (IV) and intramuscular (IM) administration, for the prevention of postpartum haemorrhage, at elective caesarean section. An open label, prospective, exploratory, randomised controlled trial.

Intervention Arm: Oxytocin; a single, 10 IU intramuscular injection following birth.
Comparator Arm: Oxytocin; a single 5 IU intravenous injection following birth.

The study is estimated to recruit 120 participants, and will be undertaken at hospitals in Australia.

Title: The effect of immediate cessation of intravenous oxytocin post birth on postpartum haemorrhage in spontaneous vaginal delivery following induction of labour with oxytocin: a comparison of three regimes.
Description:
We are investigating the best time for the midwife to stop the synthetic oxytocin infusion after a spontaneous vaginal birth. We want to investigate this topic as there is no current evidence to guide this clinical practice.

Control Arm 1; Intravenous oxytocin ceased within 15 minutes of completion of the third stage of labour.
Intervention Arm2; Intravenous oxytocin ceased 30 minutes after completion of the third stage of labour.
Intervention Arm 3; Intravenous oxytocin ceased 60 minutes after completion of the third stage of labour.

The trial will recruit 312 participants, and will take place at a hospital in Australia.

Title: A randomised controlled trial of intravenous versus intramuscular oxytocin in the management of third stage of labor.
Description:

Experimental Arm 1: Intravenous oxytocin injection 10 units immediately after delivery of the newborn.
Experimental Arm 2: Intramuscular oxytocin injection 10 units immediately after delivery of the newborn.

Study is estimated to recruit 450 participants, and will take place at a hospital in Thailand.

Title: Comparison of the efficacy of oxtyocin agonist to oxytocin in the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) in women undergoing vaginal delivery
Description:
This study is intended to compare the efficacy and safety of an oxytocin analogue and oxytocin in the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage (massive bleeding after birth) in women undergoing vaginal delivery. Oxytocin and its analogue are drugs used to contract the uterus to prevent postpartum hemorrhage. We would like to compare the effect of the drugs to lower the need for additional intervention (additional massage or other uterotonic needed) in the prevention of PPH postpartum hemorrhage.

Intervention Arm: Oxytocin; 100 microgram Intramuscular (IM) slow bolus injection of oxytocin agonist after infant is delivered.
Active Comparator: Oxytocin; 10IU (International Unit) Intramuscular (IM) bolus injection of oxytocin after infant is delivered.

The trial will recruit 720 participants, and take place at a hospital in Malaysia.

Title: Intravenous plus intramyometrial oxytocin versus intravenous cabetocin during caesarean section in prevention of post-partum hemorrhage: a randomized controlled trial

Intravenous plus intramyometrial oxytocin versus intravenous carbetocin during caesarean section in prevention of post-partum hemorrhage: a randomized controlled trial

Intervention Arm 1: Oxytocin; oxytocin 20 unit in LRS 500 ml intravenous plus oxytocin 5 unit in intramyometrial after placenta delivery
Intervention Arm 2: Carbetocin; 100 microgram intravenous after placenta delivery.

The study will recruit 50 participants, and will take place at a hospital in Thailand.

Title: A clinical trial to evaluate effects of Misoprostol by sublingual route after delivery of neonate in preventing postpatum bleeding in comparison to intramuscular injection of oxytocin
Description:
This is a randomized,double blind, active controlled parallel group trial comparing 400 microgram Misoprostol administered sublingually and 10 units oxytocin given intramuscularly to low risk women in third stage of labor after vaginal delivery. The proposed number of women to be recruited is 1200 over a 6month period (600 in each group) and the enrollment started from August2009. The primary outcome measure will be difference in the hemoglobin level in 24 hours after delivery.The secondary outcome measures will be amount of bleeding during one hour observation period after delivery, incidence of postpartum hemorrhage, duration of third stage of labor,need for additional oxytocic and manual removal of placenta, side effects and complications during 24 hour observation period. 

Intervention Arm: Misoprostol; 400ug tablets were given sublingually at the delivery of anterior shoulder of the neonate.
Comparator Arm: Oxytocin; 10 IU given intramuscularly after delivery of anterior shoulder of the neonate.

The study will enrol 600 participants, and take place at a hospital in India.

Title: Comparison between mothers at high or low risk of uterine bleeding, with regards to the effective dose of oxytocin during cesarean surgery
Description:
Oxytocin is drug of choice for achieving uterine contraction and thus preventing postpartum hemorrhage during cesarean section. Recently, there have been studies to evaluate its minimum effective dose during cesarean section. However, these have been conducted in patients at “low-risk” of uterine atony. Thus, there is no existing evidence for minimum effective dose of oxytocin to achieve adequate uterine tone during cesarean section in patients with high-risk of uterine atony. Aim:To evaluate and compare during cesarean section in non-laboring patients at high-risk versus low-risk of uterine atony, the minimum effective dose of oxytocin bolus for achieving adequate uterine tone.

Intervention Arm 1: Oxytocin; intravenously, at time of umbilical cord clamping, 3 IU dose in first patient, dose in subsequent patients decided by sequential allocation method depending on response in previous patient, ie, increased or decreased by 0.5 IU for inadequate or adequate uterine contraction at 3 minutes respectively. 
Intervention Arm 2: Oxytocin, intravenously, at time of umbilical cord clamping, 1 IU dose in first patient, dose in subsequent patients decided by sequential allocation method depending on response in previous patient, ie, increased or decreased by 0.2 IU for inadequate or adequate uterine contraction at 3 minutes respectively.

The is estimated to enrol 60 participants, and will be undertaken at a hospital in India.
Sponsor: University College of Mediacl Sciences and GTb Hospital

Title: The dose of oxytocin needed to contract uterus after delivery of baby during cesarean section, when using the dose according to weight of patient
Description:
Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) is a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality and the commonest cause of PPH is uterine atony. Oxytocin as a uterotonic is used to prevent uterine atony during cesarean section as well as vaginal delivery but higher doses of oxytocin can cause serious maternal side effects.There is significant variability in dose when we compare weight-based versus non weight-based approach and the adverse effects of oxytocin gets unnecessarily amplified in case of the excess dose while its uterotonic effect gets compromised for a deficient one. Hence weight-based oxytocin infusions may help to optimize the amount while also decreasing the side effects. There is no published data regarding weight-based doses of oxytocin infusion. 

Intervention Arm 1: Oxytocin; 0.1 IU/kg/hr weight-based, fixed-rate prophylactic oxytocin infusions
Intervention Arm 2: Oxytocin; 0.15 IU/kg/hr weight-based, fixed-rate prophylactic oxytocin infusions
Intervention Arm 3: Oxytocin; 0.2 IU/kg/hr weight-based, fixed-rate prophylactic oxytocin infusions
Intervention Arm 4: Oxytocin; 0.25IU/kg/hr weight-based, fixed-rate prophylactic oxytocin infusions
Intervention Arm 5: Oxytocin; 0.3 IU/kg/hr weight-based, fixed-rate prophylactic oxytocin infusions

The trial is estimated to enrol 55 participants, and will take place at a hospital in India.
Sponsor: University College of Medical Sciences and GTB Hospital

Title: A clinical trial to compare the effects of Misoprostol(per rectal) and Oxytocin(intravenous infusion)in reducing blood loss in women undergoing caesarean section.
Description:
A randomised double-blind well controlled clinical trial to compare the efficacy and safety of rectally administered Misoprostol and Intravenous Oxytocin infusion in preventing intraoperative and postpartum blood loss in women undergoing caesarean section. 

Intervention Arm: Misoprostol; 800 microgram given rectally after peritonium is opened during LSCS.

The study will enroll 200 participants, and will take place in India.

Title: Carbetocin versus Oxytocin for the Prevention of Postpartum Hemorrhage in Hypertensive Pregnant Women
Description:
In patient with hypertension during pregnancy there is an increased risk of PPH, but the hemodynamic changes associated with hypertension during pregnancy make the management of any kind of bleeding particularly troublesome. There are many pharmacological options for the management of PPH, oxytocin being the first line of treatment, there is yet no evidence about safety and efficacy of using carbetocin, an oxytocin agonist, in these patient. The aim of this work is to assess the effectiveness and safety of carbetocin, an oxytocin agonist, versus oxytocin in the prevention of PPH in hypertensive pregnant women.

Experimental Arm: Carbetocin; 100 μg carbetocin diluted in 10 ml of Ringer’s lactate solution injected directly into the vein over 2 min (Pabal; Ferring, Langley, UK).
Control Arm: Oxytocin; one ampoule 10 IU oxytocin (Syntocinon; Alliance, Chippenham, UK) in 1000 ringer lactate as IV drip at a rate of 125 ml/h.

The study is estimated to recuit 160 participants, and will take place in Egypt.
Sponsor: Faculty of Medicine, Suez Canal University

Title: studying the effect of different uterotonic agents in prevention of postpartum hemorrhage following cesarean section in high risk cases.
Description:
This is a comparative study between carbetocin, oxytocin and misoprostol in prevention of postpartum hemorrhage following cesarean section in high risk cases.

Intervention Arm 1: Carbetocin; 100 microgram of PAPAL (carbetocin) IV as a uterotonic agent after delivery of fetal anterior shoulder.
Intervention Arm 2: Oxytocin; 5 IU of IV bolus oxytocin then will be followed by 40 IU of oxytocin infusion on 1000 ml saline with a rate of 150 ml per hour as a uterotonic agent after delivery of fetal anterior shoulder.
Intervention Arm 3: Misoprostol; 800 microgram misoprostol rectally immediately after anesthesia and before Cesarean Section followed by 5 IU of oxytocin IV bolus immediately after delivery of anterior shoulder as a uterotonic agent.

The study will recruit 240 participants, and be undertaken at a hospital in Egypt.

Description: This double-blind randomised controlled trial, will assess the relative effectiveness of two different oxytocin regimens for the prevention/treatment of haemorrhage after a caesarean sectionExperimental Arm: Oxytocin; a single dose intravenous bolus injection of 5 IU (international units) oxytocin plus 20 IU (international units) oxytocin intravenous infusion (rate 250mls hour infused over 4 hours).Comparator Arm: Oxytocin; a single dose intravenous bolus injection of 5 IU (international units) oxytocin alone.The study will recruit 474 participants, and take place at hospitals in Australia. Title: Use of Oxytocin Different Doses and Route of Administration During Delivery to Decrease Bleeding
Description:
A randomised control trial of 3 IU intravenous oxytocin bolus with 7 IU oxytocin infusion versus 10 IU oxytocin intramuscular in the third stage of labour for the prevention of post partum hemorrhage.

Intervention Arm: 3IU Oxytocin bolus, 7IU IV Infusion; 3 IU of oxytocin will be diluted and shall be administered intravenously over 1 minute. 7 IU units of oxytocin shall be added to the IV fluid. The drug shall be given at the delivery of the anterior shoulder of the baby. IV fluid can be Ringer’s Lactate or 0.9% normal saline.
Comparator Arm: 10 IU Oxytocin IM; 10 IU Intramuscular oxytocin will be given to the mother at the delivery of anterior shoulder of the baby.

The study will enrol 320 participants, and take place at a hospital in India.

Title: Prevention of Postpartum Hemorrhage with Oxytocin versus Ergometrine Plus Oxytocin in the third stage of labor
Description:
A study into the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage with oxytocin versus ergometrine Plus oxytocin in the third stage of labor.

Active Comparator: combination of oxytocin 20 IU diluted in 1 l in 5%D/N/2 intravenous drip infusion of 120 ml/h and ergometrine 0.2 mg (1ml) intravenous injection.
Placebo Comparator: oxytocin 20 IU diluted in 1 l in 5%D/N/2 intravenous drip infusion of 120 ml/h and normal saline 1 ml (placebo) intravenous injection.

The study will recruit 323 participants, and will take place in Thailand.

Title: Oxytocin intravenous bolus injection versus standard Intravenous infusion of oxytocin during cesarean section for prevention of post partum bleeding
Description:
Various uterotonics have been used over the years. Oxytocin, ergometrine, misoprostol and PGF2-alpha have been extensively studied. However the optimal route and dose of these drugs are still being studied. In view of the smaller dose of oxytocin required, we propose to conduct a randomised control trial on 3 IU oxytocin IV bolus over one minute with 7 units oxytocin infusion vs 10 IU oxytocin infusion during cesarean section for the prevention of post partum hemorrhage.

Intervention Arm: 3 IU Oxytocin Bolus With 7 IU Oxytocin Infusion; 3 IU of oxytocin will be diluted and shall be administered intravenously over 1 minute. 7 IU units of oxytocin shall be added to the IV fluid. The drug shall be given at the delivery of the anterior shoulder of the baby. 
Comparator Arm: 10 IU Oxytocin Infusion During Cesarean Section; 10 IU oxytocin will be added to the intravenous infusion.

The study will recruit 250 participants, and will take place at a hospital in India.
Sponsor: BLDE Deemed to be UniversityShri BM Patil Medical College Hospital and Research Center

Title: A study to compare the effectiveness of intravenous oxytocin with intramuscular oxytocin given at the third stage of labour at preventing bleeding at vaginal birth
Description:
By giving the woman an injection containing artificial oxytocin, it can help speed up the delivery of the placenta and prevent excess bleeding. This injection can be given a number of ways, such as directly into the bloodstream or into muscle, however it is not known which is the most effective. The aim of this study is to find out the most effective technique of giving oxytocin to women in labour to prevent bleeding.

Intervention Arm 1: Oxytocin; Participants will receive 1ml 10IU oxytocin intramuscularly and 1ml 0.9% normal saline as placebo intravenously immediately after the delivery of the baby and before the delivery of the placenta at vaginal delivery.
Invervention Arm 2: Oxytocin; Participants will receive 1ml 10IU oxytocin intravenously and 1ml 0.9% normal saline as placebo intramuscularly immediately after the delivery of the baby and before the delivery of the placenta at vaginal delivery.

The study will recruit 1000 participants, and will be undertaken at hospitals in Ireland.
Sponsor: Coombe Women and Infants University Hospital

Title: Efficacy of intravenous 100 mcg carbetocin versus intravenous 5 units oxytocin for prevention of immediate postpartum hemorrhage after normal vagina delivery among high risk prenancies; a tripple-blinded randomized controlled trial
Description:
Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) is the most important obstetrics complication. Prevention of PPH based on administration of uterotonic drugs, controlled cord traction and uterine massage. Oxytocin is the first line drug which is recommended for PPH prevention as its high efficacy but short duration of action. Carbetocin (Oxytocin agonist) is an alternative drugs approved for PPH prevention. The more advantage of this drug is its long duration of action; therefore only single dose is adequate. This study aims to determine the efficacy of carbetocin for PPH prevention compared with standard oxytocin in randomized controlled trial.

Intervention Arm 1: Oxytocin; 5 IU IV slow push.
Intervention Arm 2: Carbetocin; 100 mcg IV slowly push

The study will recruit 352 participants, and take place at a hospital in Thailand.

Title: ACTIVE MANAGEMENT OF THE THIRD STAGE OF LABOUR WITHOUT CONTROLLED CORD TRACTION FOR PREVENTING POSTPARTUM HAEMORRHAGE: A RANDOMIZED NON-INFERIORITY CONTROLLED TRIAL
Description: The third stage of labour refers to the period between birth of the baby and complete expulsion of the placenta. Some degree of blood loss occurs after the birth of the baby due to separation of the placenta. This period is a risky period because uterus may not contract well after birth and heavy blood loss can endanger the life of the mother. Active management of the third stage of labour (AMTSL) reduces the occurrence of severe postpartum haemorrhage by approximately 60-70%. Active management consists of several interventions packaged together and the relative contribution of each of the components is unknown. Controlled cord traction is one of those components that require training in manual skill for it to be performed appropriately. If it is possible to dispense with controlled cord traction without losing efficacy it would have major implications for effective management of the third stage of labour at peripheral levels of health care.Experimental Arm: Oxytocin; uterotonic (oxytocin 10 IU IM) injection after delivery of the baby, cord clamping and cutting at approximately 3 minutes after birth.Active Comparator: Oxytocin; uterotonic injection (oxytocin 10 IU IM), controlled cord traction following observation of uterine contraction and cord clamping and cutting at approximately 3 minutes after birth.The trial will recruit 24390 participants, and be undertaken at 16 hospitals and two primary health-care centres in Egypt, South Africa, Thailand, Ugand, Philippines, Kenya, India and Argentina.
Locations: Egypt; South Africa; Thailand; Uganda; Philippines; Kenya; India; Argentina

Title: Comparison of postpartum blood loss between intravenous oxytocin and intravenous methylergometrine maleate during third stage of labor

Title: Prevention of Postpartum Hemorrhage With Tranexamic Acid
Description:
In part 1 of the study, the investigators conducted a prospective, open-label, dose finding pharmacokinetic (PK) study in 43 pregnant 3rd trimester women scheduled for non-emergent cesarean section.

The investigators administered three doses of the drug (5 mg/kg, 10 mg/kg and 15 mg/kg) in an escalating fashion by cohort with the lowest dose first. The drug was administered intravenously at the time of umbilical cord clamping for a non-emergent cesarean section. A maximum of 1 g was administered. TXA serum levels at several time points after delivery were assayed to see if they reach the target plasma concentration of 10 ug/mL. A PK model was constructed for determining the optimal TXA dose administered at parturition.

In part 2 of the study, the investigators aim to compare PKPD endpoints using prophylactic TXA via IV and IM routes administered pre-cord clamp. The investigators will administer 1 g TXA within 10 minutes of skin incision via intravenous infusion (up to n=15), intravenous bolus \< 2 minutes (up to n=15) and intramuscular injection (up to n=15). The investigators will target women undergoing scheduled cesarean delivery \> 34 weeks gestation, women undergoing vaginal delivery \> 34 weeks of gestation and morbidly obese women (BMI\>=40) undergoing either a vaginal or cesarean delivery. The investigators will use advanced modeling techniques to determine time to achieve PKPD targets and duration remaining at those targets. The goal will be to determine how the optimal dose may vary if route of administration is modified. The investigators plan to enroll 45 patients in addition to the 43 that were enrolled during part 1. Our goal is to 30 participants, but the investigators will enroll 45 to account for lost to follow-up. The investigators also aim to enroll 30 patients undergoing vaginal delivery and 30 morbidly obese women (BMI \>= 40) undergoing either a vaginal or cesarean delivery but the investigators will enroll 45 patients for each of these groups to account for loss to follow up. In addition, the investigators will enroll 30 pregnant patients receiving no medication acting as the control group, but the investigators will enroll 45 to account for loss to follow up.

REBOA in Life-threatening Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH) in Uganda
Description:
Background Maternal mortality rates in many low-income countries (LMICs) remain high. The most prominent cause is bleeding after birth, called postpartum haemorrhage (PPH). In a recent report from Uganda, bleeding is the cause of 42% of all maternal deaths in Uganda.

Large parts of the monitoring of mothers during active management of third stage of labour is aiming to prevent and early detect PPH and take relevant actions. In spite of this and sometimes in referring mothers to tertiary hospitals, mothers will end up in a challenging condition where quick action is needed. A new method has proven successful for such instances, the Resuscitative Endovascular Balloon Occlusion of the Aorta (REBOA). This is a procedure commonly used for trauma of the lower part of the body but rarely used for PPH. A balloon catheter is inserted via the femoral artery in the groin into the aorta and then being inflated. This will prevent blood from passing to the lower part of the body, including the uterus. It will stop the bleeding and allow for the obstetrician to take relevant action. This is a safe procedure for up to 1 hour of balloon occlusion time including repeated short balloon deflations.

Objective To assess the efficacy and safety of Resuscitative Endovascular Balloon Occlusion of the Aorta (REBOA) in life-threatening postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) in reducing adverse maternal outcome compared to standard of care in Uganda.

Study design, setting and population A phase IIb/III, open label, 1:1 randomized clinical trial will be conducted at Kawempe National Referral Hospital, Kampala, Uganda, to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Resuscitative Endovascular Balloon Occlusion of the Aorta (REBOA) in life-threatening postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) in reducing adverse maternal outcome compared to standard of care. The inclusion criteria are: a) women with life-threatening PPH and a systolic blood pressure equal to or less than 80 mmHg, b) written consent. The exclusion criterion is prior cardiac arrest or intra-abdominal pregnancy. The sample size of the trial will be 212 participants. Enrolment will follow a group sequential design approach with two interim analyses at 50% and 85% of the total sample size, and a final analysis with full sample size.

Utility of the study It is crucial to explore alternative modalities that could prevent adverse maternal outcomes in life-threatening postpartum haemorrhage in Uganda and the rest of the world.

Title: Oxytocin Maintenance Infusion in Labouring Women Undergoing Cesarean Delivery: an Up-down Sequential Allocation Study
Description:
This study is designed to determine the minimal effective oxytocin maintenance infusion required in labouring women undergoing cesarean delivery to achieve the best effect. Oxytocin is a drug that is routinely used to help the uterus to contract and keep it contracted after delivery. Consequently, it will help to reduce blood loss after delivery. In order to determine the minimal effective dose, the investigators will conduct a dose-finding study. The first patient will receive a set oxytocin infusion. The next patient's infusion dose of oxytocin, will either increase or decrease, depending on how the previous patient responds in terms of uterine tone. If the response is satisfactory with the infusion dose used, the next patient will either receive the same infusion dose or it will be decreased depending on a probability of 1:9. If the response is not satisfactory, then the infusion dose will increase for the next patient. The dose for each patient will be determined based on the results of the uterine contraction of the previous patient.

The investigators hypothesize that the ED90 of the oxytocin infusion rate to maintain adequate uterine tone in labouring women with induced or augmented labour undergoing cesarean delivery, following an initial effective bolus dose, would be lower than 0.74 IU/min (44 IU/h), which was found as the ED90 in a previous study, without an initial bolus dose prior to the infusion.

Oxytocin Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics
Description:
Oxytocin is the first-line drug to promote contraction of the uterus and prevent atony immediately after delivery. Nonetheless, unpredictable uterine atony refractory to oxytocin affects roughly 250,000 parturients annually in the U.S. and rates are increasing. This two-part study will measure the action of oxytocin at cesarean delivery. The first part will measure the pharmacokinetics of a single intravenous (IV) dose of deuterium-labeled oxytocin. The second part will measure the pharmacodynamics of all plasma oxytocin to see how concentrations correspond to the contractile effect on the uterus.

After delivery of the fetus, study subjects will receive a bolus of IV deuterated oxytocin followed by an unlabeled oxytocin infusion. Venous blood samples drawn at multiple time points (within 1 hour after delivery) will be analyzed for plasma concentrations of labeled and unlabeled (endogenous + exogenous infused) oxytocin over time. Plasma concentrations will be compared with 0-10 uterine tone scores measuring uterine contraction strength, to describe the concentration-effect relationship.

The goal of this study is to define both the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of oxytocin in parturients to help identify the cause(s) of failed first-line oxytocin therapy.

Title: Comparing the Dose-response Profiles of Uterotonics After Initial Carbetocin Administration - an Ex-vivo Study in Desensitized Human Myometrium
Description:
This study will investigate the effects of drugs called "uterotonics" that help with the contraction of the uterus after a baby is born. This uterine contraction is very important to stop the bleeding after delivery. An uncontracted uterine state is called "uterine atony", which can lead to an excessive amount of post-delivery bleeding. Carbetocin is an uterotonic drug that works well to prevent post-delivery bleeding. In some cases, carbetocin is not enough to contract the uterus, and ongoing bleeding continues. When that happens, there are other uterotonic medications that can be used. In this study, we aim to find which uterotonic drug, amongst those available (oxytocin, carbetocin, ergometrine or carboprost), is more effective to lower the risk of post-delivery bleeding once carbetocin has already been administered.

This study will be done by using a very small sample of uterine tissue, taken from the incision site, following delivery by cesarean section. The sample is taken to the laboratory and will be exposed to carbetocin followed by other uterotonic drugs. The information obtained from this study will help modify the treatment for uterine atony and post-delivery bleeding to lower the risk further.

Title: Synbiotics in Patients at RIsk fOr Preterm Birth
Description:
Prematurity remains the main cause of death and serious health problems in new-borns. Besides the need for hospitalization and medical interventions in the first weeks or months of the new-borns' life, prematurity can cause long-lasting health problems (e.g. multiple hospital admissions, developmental delay, learning difficulties, motor delay, hearing or eye problems, ...). Moreover, prematurity places an enormous economic burden on the society. Aside from the medical problems and the financial cost, the emotional stress and psychological impact on the parents, siblings and other family members should not be underestimated.

Previous preterm delivery (before 37 weeks of pregnancy) increases the risk for recurrent preterm delivery in a subsequent pregnancy. Therefore, these women should be considered as 'high risk' for preterm birth.

Infections ascending from the vagina may be an important cause of preterm delivery in certain cases. Some women have an abnormal vaginal microbiome and are therefore at risk for infections and preterm birth. On the other hand, the vaginal flora is more stable and resistant to infections in healthy pregnant women who deliver at term (after 37 weeks of gestation).

Synbiotics are a mixture containing probiotics and prebiotics. Probiotics are living bacteria with potential beneficial effects that can be used safely in pregnancy, while prebiotics are consumed by the bacteria. It is known that probiotics, when used for a long period of time, can maintain a healthy and stable vaginal flora that may protect against infections. In this study, pregnant patients with a history of preterm birth will be included in the first trimester of pregnancy to start with synbiotics or placebo. The investigators will examine the effect of synbiotics on the vaginal flora and on the pregnancy duration. The hypothesis is that synbiotics, when started early in the pregnancy, can change the disturbed vaginal flora into a stable micro-environment.
